purpose: Trace the Prime scheduler transition after an IOS interrupt wakes the main guest thread during a retrace wait.

instrumentation.change: Diagnostic-only [prime-ipc-context-switch] trace records guest running/current context and interrupted/callback LR and r1 when Prime's IPC handler changes the selected thread. No register file is copied back.
Diagnostic-only [prime-vi-switch] trace checks whether the Prime VI handler itself changes the running thread.
Existing bounded wait/scheduler/context diagnostics include wait caller LR and OSContext values.
Existing bounded IPC handler and ioctlv traces.

runtime.visual_capture: No capture was taken in this run; no real game screen is confirmed.
observations: The seventh logged guest yield is at caller LR 0x803C41DC, with wait counter 2; no matching reschedule-return trace appears.
The Prime scheduler moves from running context 0 to 0x8060B418 while processing the IOS interrupt.
At that transition the interrupted callback began with LR 0x804E6D08 and r1 0x80699DA0, but the callback returned with LR 0 and r1 0x8069A0B0, the interrupt stack.
The process continues advancing VI retraces, but the game-thread wait has no recorded return.
runtime.failed_trial: A temporary runtime experiment copied the callback CpuContext back after the thread-pointer change. It did not resume the wait and left the callback register file at LR=0/r1=0x8069A0B0; that state mutation was removed from the final build.

interpretation: The wake queue and global scheduler state advance, but the static translated guest stack does not resume at a verified continuation. The callback context is not a valid replacement CPU register file after its generated callers return, so copying it back is rejected. This is evidence of an interrupt/thread context-transfer problem; it does not identify the complete fix.
next: Trace where Prime's saved OSContext and callback CpuContext diverge through 0x804E6BD4/0x804E01C4 and the outer translated call boundary. Implement a resumable guest context transfer only after its continuation and register ownership are established; then rerun the runtime and confirm a real frame.
